note: Every source this publication draws on, and its ingestion state. The register exists so a reader can tell — without asking — whether a fact reached the graph from the primary text or by way of somebody else's reading of it. In this first release NO source has been ingested directly from a regulator. Everything in the seed graph is second-hand from a sibling sgit.ai site, and every node says so.

ingestion_states.label: Primary
ingestion_states.definition: Frozen from the issuing body's own artefact, hashed, with quotes anchored to byte offsets in that copy.

ingestion_states.label: Secondary
ingestion_states.definition: Taken from another publication's reading of a primary source. Usable, and always labelled — a secondary fact can never be presented as anchored.

ingestion_states.label: Planned
ingestion_states.definition: Named as in scope for the beat, with nothing ingested yet.

sources.title: Staleness in the wild — the EU AI Act's consolidated text
sources.note: This site's own published account. Dated and public, but it is a reading of the regulation, not the regulation.

sources.title: Article 26(5) — nine questions, five unanswered
sources.note: A worked provision study. Four of its five unanswered questions are not restated here because their wording was not carried across — see q-unnamed-four, which records that absence rather than inventing them.

sources.title: The EU AI Act regulation graph — 1,523 nodes, 1,944 edges
sources.note: Parsed from official Formex XML with SHA-256 verification at every provenance point. The nearest thing to a primary ingestion available to this publication today — but it is that site's parse, not this one's.

sources.title: The established edge set
sources.note: Not a news source. The grammar this beat's ontology inherits its four reused edges from.

sources.title: The risk ontology — 42 concepts
sources.note: Not a news source. The concept register this beat defers to for anything risk-shaped rather than restating.

planned.why: The primary artefact for any instrument this beat covers. Freezing and hashing these is what turns every secondary fact above into a primary one.
planned.blocked_on: An ingestion path that fetches, freezes, hashes and anchors — the piece this release does not have.

planned.class: News and press releases issued by regulatory and supervisory bodies
planned.why: Named by the commissioning brief as the beat's most interesting source class: dated, attributable, issued by the body with authority over the text.
planned.blocked_on: Same ingestion path. Also needs a per-body register so a publication can be attributed to a body rather than to a URL.

planned.why: Where an obligation is actually made operable, and where silent republication is most common — the condition the staleness wire exists to catch.
planned.blocked_on: Ingestion path, plus a change-detection loop that re-fetches on a cadence.

planned.class: Open consultations and their response documents
planned.why: Consultations state the questions a body knows it has not answered. That is the absence board's richest input and it is published voluntarily.
The record of what a body actually does, as against what its text says it may do.
